links.comparator_used: Default-threshold classifiers trained on the original imbalanced data without resampling
links.effect: SMOTE improved minority-class recognition relative to default-threshold models; no numeric values reported in the abstract
links.tradeoff: SMOTE altered classification behavior and the class distribution, unlike cost-sensitive threshold optimization, which preserved real-world prevalence.
links.quote: SMOTE improved minority-class recognition but altered classification behavior.

links.comparator_used: Default-threshold classification (standard default decision threshold) across ten ML classifiers
links.outcome: Balanced performance and identification of non-survivors (specificity, sensitivity, balanced accuracy)
links.effect: Threshold-optimized SVM: specificity 0.857, sensitivity 0.914, balanced accuracy 0.886, correctly identified 18 of 21 non-survivors; McNemar testing showed significant classification changes after threshold optimization for most classifiers
links.quote: Cost-sensitive threshold optimization improved balanced performance without changing the original class distribution.
